questions.question: How do you write acceptance criteria for a reporting requirement?
questions.shortAnswer: Make each criterion observable and testable with clear inputs, expected output, filters and edge cases.
questions.explanation: Acceptance criteria reduce ambiguity and help analysts, developers and business users agree on “done.”
questions.example: “Selecting March and North region updates total sales and order count; both reconcile to the approved source within the agreed rule.”
commonMistakes: Avoid vague criteria such as “dashboard should be user-friendly.”
questions.followUp: Who should approve the KPI definition and reconciliation tolerance?

questions.question: Two stakeholders request conflicting definitions for the same KPI. What do you do?
questions.shortAnswer: Document both definitions, clarify decisions they support and get the accountable metric owner to approve a standard or labelled variants.
questions.explanation: Do not silently choose one. A single label with multiple calculations undermines trust.

questions.question: What should a reliable daily MIS report include besides the figures?
questions.shortAnswer: Reporting period, source/freshness timestamp, metric definitions, exceptions/data-quality status and the intended audience/action.
questions.explanation: Context helps readers interpret changes and spot stale or incomplete data. Keep the report concise and avoid unnecessary decoration.
questions.example: A header shows report date and last refresh, followed by KPIs, variances, top exceptions and owner/actions.

questions.question: How do you perform user acceptance testing (UAT) for a dashboard?
questions.shortAnswer: Use agreed scenarios and expected results, verify calculations and interactions with business users, log defects and obtain sign-off.
questions.explanation: UAT should validate real user requirements, not only that the page opens. Include normal cases, edge cases and access rules.

questions.question: What is the difference between a business requirement and a technical solution?
questions.shortAnswer: A business requirement states the need or outcome; a technical solution describes how the system will deliver it.

questions.question: A monthly report is frequently delayed. How would you investigate and improve it?
questions.shortAnswer: Map the workflow and dependencies, measure delays, identify the bottleneck, then test one targeted improvement.
questions.explanation: Separate data availability delays from manual consolidation, validation, approvals and distribution. Set owners and track before/after timing.

questions.question: How can you explain a technical idea when your English is limited?

questions.question: What can you say when you need time to think during an interview?
questions.shortAnswer: Use one polite sentence to request a moment, then organize the answer.

questions.question: How do you ask an interviewer to clarify an ambiguous question?
questions.shortAnswer: Repeat the part you understood and ask which condition or outcome they want you to focus on.

questions.question: How can you keep a behavioural answer under one minute?

questions.question: How would you politely correct yourself after giving an incorrect answer?

questions.question: How do you describe a skill without saying you are an expert?

questions.question: How should you explain that a portfolio project uses synthetic data?
questions.shortAnswer: State it openly, explain why it is used and focus on the analytical workflow, validation and product decisions it demonstrates.

questions.question: How do you explain the limitations of a one-snapshot inventory dataset?
questions.shortAnswer: It can describe risk at that snapshot, but cannot support a reliable historical trend without multiple comparable snapshots.

questions.question: How would you describe your role when part of a portfolio project was planned but not deployed?

questions.question: How would you walk through a project data model in an interview?
questions.shortAnswer: State the grain of the fact table, describe dimension keys, explain relationships and name the main measures.

questions.question: What can you safely claim if the repository has automated tests?
